channel.title: Ramen Reviews on Eisuke Hirota
channel.description: Recent content in Ramen Reviews on Eisuke Hirota

item.title: Burari - Chicken Paitan Classic
item.description:
• Price: ¥990
  • Rating: 9/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-18
  • Review: The soup is the star of the dish - crazily gelatinous and really clings to the noodles and your palate, but not to the point of being overbearing. Chashu, celery, scallions, egg, and the red pepper add a nice burst of flavor and appeal.

item.title: Charume - Chuuka Soba w/ Wontons
item.description:
• Price: ¥1200
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-01-08
  • Review: classic bowl with seafood broth and a soy sauce base. everything is really clean and refreshing, and the wontons add a fresh twist. for me, the star is the chicken chashu which has a clean fattyness w/ a slight spice aftertaste that shines through the rest of the bowl. overall, a great classic example of chuuka soba w/ a seafood broth.

item.title: Downtown - Mushroom Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $15
  • Rating: 5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-04-01
  • Review: overall just tastes like shin ramyun, idk how else to describe it. This was a vegan option at an american restaurant so I was like “why not.” The noodles were decent, but the soup is a mushroom base that only reminds me of shin. It’s pretty sad as a ramen, and even more so as a vegan option. I pity vegetarians/vegans who get served this. Overall the toppings don’t make sense either, though the mushrooms were nice. I like shin, don’t get me wrong. But I only like it as an instant ramen option, not as a “go outside to try food at a restaurant” type of ramen. It’s the only ramen so far which I didn’t finish and made my friend eat instead. I mean, I had low expectations and it met my low bar.

item.title: Edomondo - Jiro-style Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥950
  • Rating: 7.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-21
  • Review: (for the price, you can get small/med/large portion of noods for and i accidentally got a large which now I’m in a food coma) the broth is a bit salty but b/c you can get a buttload of toppings for free (bean sprouts, cabbage, raw garlic), it easily cuts thru w/ the thick noodles. theres a quail egg and a really tender chashu. the amount adds up to probs like 2000 calories or smth but flavorwise its really heavy. its a nice little shop tho, tons of retro video game motifs. i was eating while listening to final fantasy music and looking at ryu and slime on a sign.

item.title: Hatori - Ginger Shoyu Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥950
  • Rating: 9/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-17
  • Review: Clean shoyu soup base with a sharp ginger topping accent. The chashu pork is melt-in-your-mouth tender and the other toppings were executed well. For the price, 9/10.

item.title: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka - Miso Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $20
  • Rating: 7/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-07-19
  • Review: a pretty classic bowl of miso. I’m not knowledgeable on hokkaido ramen and reading online I’m still clueless, so my view might be biased here. anyway, it was a decent bowl: noods, soup, bamboo shoots all good. I’d have preferred softer and juicer chashu, a more miso-centric soup (was slighlty weak), and maybe fresher woodear mushrooms (felt a bit bland). That being said, I think the quality of this for being in america is better than I expected (especially for a chain restaurant), and I overall enjoyed it. Definitely a great starter for anyone wanting to eat more traditional ramen.

item.title: Jigemon Champon - Spicy Miso
item.description:
• Price: ¥980
  • Rating: 6.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-28
  • Review: the first sip of the soup brings a very filling flavor of the rich spicy miso broth. unfortunately , this soup is really rich the more you eat, the more overwhelming it becomes. on top of that, the toppings are really standard flavor that one’d expect for a cheaper bowl of ramen.

item.title: Kaze no Jin - Iekei-style Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥1000
  • Rating: 7.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-24
  • Review: supposedly popular w/ some students who attend tokyo uni (japans #1 uni) and i can see the appeal - cheap and volumey. nothing particular stands out though, the toppings are the iekei style ones (bean sprouts cabbage onions which are great) and chashu (which was mediocre at best). For a broke college student who also needs the time for studying/part-time job, a quick and filling bowl for ¥1000 here is probably the best one can get.

item.title: Kikanbou - Karashibi Miso Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥1130
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-08-13
  • Review: been here b4 but didn’t review last time, so here’s a review. this place is miso ramen but it’s spicy as shit. you can customize the heat level and numbness level; I’m weak so I did medium spice and low numbness but I think I could’ve gone higher. Along w/ that, it comes with a fatty piece of chashu and stir fried bean sprouts and chinese chives. Everything is done amazingly well, the thicker noodles help catch the strong soup and the whole bowl packs a punch. Not to mention the toppings are all top notch and also catch the strong soup. My only gripe is I’d need to order an additional bowl of rice to dump into all the soup goodness once I’m done with the noods. I’ll def try that next time.

item.title: Menya Hidamari - Shio Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥950
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-25
  • Review: seafood based shio broth that was ultra clean along w/ a bright velvety oil that coats everything well. the saffron and yuzu toppings add a nice cut thru the oil, and the two types of chashu (fatty and lean) make for a nice overall balance in the dish. For shio ramen lovers, the rating would be higher, but even for someone like me who doesn’t like shio ramen that much, it was really good.

item.title: Menya Usagi - Tantan Zousui Set
item.description:
• Price: ¥1230
  • Rating: 8.75/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-01-18
  • Review: tantanmen (based off the chinese dish dandanmian) is (technically) a ramen that adds a sesame sauce to the bowl of soup, serving a more sauce-like experience rather than the conventional soup that one is used to. This bowl has stirfried minced meat along w/ the sichuan-inspired chili oil featuring ma (numbness) and la (spicyness). Just based off this complex melody of flavors, and a low hydration noodle that maintains its firmness and doesn’t get soggy, I’d give an 8 already. HOWEVER, I think the star is truly the sauce+soup, and what’s great about the zousui set is that the bowl comes with rice and an onsen tamago (kinda like a poached egg). Once you finish the noods, you can add the rice and eggs into the soup and mix together, creating a spicy concotion that fully captures the spice, numbness, and umami from the soup. For this shime (conclusion), I give an increased score.

item.title: Menya Yoshi - Special Shoyu Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥1400
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-23
  • Review: staff are friendly for deaf/hearing-impaired people which is great since you don’t find many inclusive places like this in jpn. also, usually when one imagines ramen they’d think of loudass busy places (stereotypically terrible for first dates) but this was quiet and tranquil. I found each topping fascinatingly fresh and explosive in flavor, especially the chicken chashu. the soup is a flavorful and clean seafood-based shoyu. the star is the velvety and clean chicken oil they use that enhances everything. the main downside is the broth is slighlty too salty, so I had to reset my palate w/ water a few times. Adding yuzu koshou halfway thru the bowl was a great flavor change and absolutely remade how I viewed the bowl, usually I add white pepper but the guy next to me added yuzu koshou so I did too.

item.title: Naoji - Seabura Chuuka Soba
item.description:
• Price: ¥980
  • Rating: 8.25/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-01-15
  • Review: this is chuuka soba that has a topping of raw diced onions and pork back fat (seabura) pieces. you’d imagine it to be very filling and heavy, but because of the light broth and raw onions, it cuts thru the fat well, leading to a very strong impactful bowl without weighing you down. very nice, though I wasn’t a huge fan of how the other toppings (chashu + menma) were.

item.title: Red White Boneless Ramen - Red Hot Miso Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $20
  • Rating: 6.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-06-29
  • Review: this is probs the second vegetarian ramen I’ve had. Flavor was not bad, and actually pretty decent. Unfortunately, it’s kinda one dimensional and not surprising. The toppings are interesting but not in a positive way. The fact that it’s vegetarian is nice, but overall there are ways to make it better without using tofu as a meat substitute. It’s kinda pathetic that people still use tofu as a meat substitute bc it’s really more than that. menma, woodear mushrooms, seaweed are more classic, add better texture, and would really suit a miso ramen. tofu is still fine here (given that tofu is often found in miso soup), but I didn’t enjoy the taste of the firm tofu (which is pretty common compared to sofu tofu). Idk why there’s a decent line for this place, 6.5/10.

item.title: Shichimencho - Ajitama Shoyu Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥970
  • Rating: 8/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-26
  • Review: textbook definition of classic shoyu ramen with a bit of tweaks: seafood broth, lean tender chashu, and straight up bamboo shoots instead of menma (this is great imo the star of the dish). Great bowl of ramen, classic flavors.

item.title: Shinshyuu - Tonkotsu Miso
item.description:
• Price: ¥1030
  • Rating: 6/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-20
  • Review: individually, all the components work well but nothing particularly amazing. the chashu and egg are average, and what brings the bowl down is the broth thats too salty. perhaps this is just an unlucky batch w/ too much miso added, but overall it makes the ramen overbearing. also the alkali flavor is somehow pretty strong in the noods, maybe the strong soup is causing the noods to taste too strong.

item.title: WakuWaku Ramen - Signature Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $18
  • Rating: 6/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-05-30
  • Review: (First, I’ll preface that the ramen comes w a side of tonkatsu, but I’m only giving a review for the ramen) Why is there god damn corn? Anyway, now that that’s out of the way: I think this is pretty average or mediocre. The individual components are decent, but there’s a lot of improvements possible. The soup is kinda thin, both in terms of strength and saltiness. One can also consider the funkiness too weak as well, but that’s preference. The noods were probs too alkali-tasting and were overcooked, which I think is the opposite of what you want from tonkotsu style ramen. I think the scallion topping was nice and unique, and the bok choy is reasonable. The chili oil was also interesting but lacked punch. The bowl overall felt muted, and could have had additional brightness, either thru some more acid added from a topping or potentially as an extra flavor component to the chili oil. Else, don’t add the chili oil at all, and instead let the customer add if they want. I say this b/c the chili oil got repetitive real fast. Lastly, despite being the “signature” ramen, nothing felt unique nor stood out to be defined as an “identity.”

item.title: Yume wo Katare - Jiro-style Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $18
  • Rating: 8/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-05-24
  • Review: my second time trying jiro, this time in cambridge. overall, a really balanced bowl, you ofc have everything you expect, super strong garlicky soup w/ tons of oil and flavor, the noodles and chashu had great texture, and overall very filling. Probably one of the best bowls of ramen I’ve had in America. My only gripe is that I couldn’t really customize the toppings: they just assume you want everything in a “moderate” amount. I definitely wanted a lighter soup w/ a shit ton more veggies as that style would help to take in this heavy monstrosity. that being said, this bowl was nonetheless solid, and the shop had an interesting atmosphere where customers can shout out their “dreams” if they finish their entire bowl (including the soup). I didn’t participate in that, I was just god damn hungry.
